name: Panasa Puttu Koora
instructions: 1. Peel the raw jackfruit, remove the hard core, and grate or finely chop it into small bits. Soak in water with a pinch of turmeric to prevent discoloration.
2. Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pan and add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, and curry leaves.
3. Add chopped onions and green chilies, sautéing until the onions turn translucent.
4. Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and cook until the raw smell disappears.
5. Add the drained jackfruit pieces, turmeric powder, and salt. Cover and cook on low heat until the jackfruit is tender.
6. Add red chili powder and coriander powder. Sauté on medium-high heat to allow the spices to coat the jackfruit and develop a slightly roasted texture.
7. Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and optional grated coconut, then serve hot with steamed rice or jowar roti.
description: Often referred to as 'Vegetarian Mutton' due to its meaty texture, Panasa Puttu Koora is a prized delicacy in Andhra Pradesh, especially during the jackfruit season. It reflects the coastal and agrarian traditions of the state, showcasing how versatile raw produce can be transformed into a flavor-packed, spicy, and rustic curry.
